N1-calendar.beat: B06 (S06, type 2) · also carries S04.2 / S07.2 in the plan
narration: S06.1 At September's average mortgage rate, 6.86 percent, the monthly payment for principal and interest is the figure on screen.
S06.3 Each payment pays the balance down a little, slowly at first, and faster later on.
N1-calendar.muted_read: Each page of the calendar is one monthly payment ($2,362/month, principal + interest, illustrative); as the pages flip, the loan stack slides along the payments and its top draws the balance: it falls slowly at first and faster later.

narration: S10.4 Every month after that, we compare the balance with the value, and stop the clock the first time the loan is 80 percent or less.
S10.5 Each bar here is one purchase month, and its height shows how long that took.
N3-fold.muted_read: One buyer's calendar stops when the loan stack reaches the 80% mark on the home's value; then every purchase month's line folds into a bar standing at its purchase month, and the bar's height is how many months that month took to reach 80% on paper.

narration: S13.1 The typical case also hides a long tail.
S13.2 About 1 in 7 purchase months took more than 5 years.
S13.3 They sit together in one stretch of the grid, the months just before and during the national price slump.
N2-bars.muted_read: Back on the grid, the bars over 60 months turn warn; they are few (about 1 in 7), and they sit together in one stretch of purchase months (2005–2009), under the part of the national price index that peaks and falls.
